div.head: II Atr 7
div.ab: Si dicatur in compatriota, quod furtum fecerit uel hominem occiderit, et hoc dicat unus sceidmannus et unus landesmannus, tunc non sit aliqua negatione dignus.
⁊ gif man secge on landesmann, þæt he orf stæle oððon man sloge, ⁊ hit secge an sceiðman ⁊ an landesman, ðonne ne beo he nane[s] andsæces wyrðe.
[Be landesmannes tyhte.] [Ld] ⁊ gif man secge on landesmann þæt he orf stæle oððon man sloge, ⁊ hit secge an sceiðman ⁊ an landesman, ðonne ne beo he nane[s] andsæces wyrðe.

(Von Klage gegen einen [Englischen] Landesunterthan. Ld) Und wenn ein Landesangehöriger angeklagt wird, dass er Vieh gestohlen oder einen Menschen erschlagen habe, und dies sagt [eidlich] aus Ein Schiffsmann [der Nordleute] und Ein Landesangehöriger, dann werde [Verklagt]er zu keinem Reinigungsbeweise zugelassen.

(Of a charge against an [English] native. Ld) And if a native is accused of having stolen cattle or killed a man, and one shipman [of the Northmen] and one native say so [on oath], then let [the accused] not be allowed any denial.

And if a man of our country is charged with having stolen cattle or with having slain anyone, and the charge is brought by one Viking and one man belonging to this country, he shall not be entitled to make any denial.
And if anyone charges a man of our country that he stole cattle or slew a man, and the charge is brought by one viking and one man of this country, he is then to be entitled to no denial.
div.note: B's ‘scæle’ for ‘stæle’; ‘nanes’ is Ld's reading (B ‘nan ei’).
literally, “ship-man”, the word for ship being an Old Norse one.
This means that he would have to go to the ordeal to clear himself.
